about: M1 preregistration (design: the R1 turns toward what its own camera sees). Written after the val run and before the test run; the test run loads it, refuses to run if any file hashed below changed or its result exists, and evaluates the criteria below once.

criteria.a: median facing error over the last 6 s, paired camera - truth_lag: 95% CI within [-3, +3] deg
criteria.b: camera and truth_lag both beat blind on it: blind - camera and blind - truth_lag have 95% CIs above 0
criteria.c: time to face within 15 deg, paired camera - truth_lag: 95% CI upper bound <= 0.5 s
criteria.d: shuffled is no better than blind: blind - shuffled (facing error) has a 95% CI lower bound <= 0
criteria.e: empty ring (camera): a turn command on <= 2% of control ticks, pooled over bouts

statistics: per bout: facing error = |true bearing of the opponent's pelvis from the R1's pelvis heading| (env.true_bearing) at every 20 ms tick; its median over t > 6 s; time to face = the first tick with facing error <= 15 deg (never: 12 s). Paired differences: r1gym/stats.py cluster_paired_diff, clusters (clip, start draw), 4000 resamples, seed 0, over the bouts both settings survived; empty ring: ticks with |wz command| > 0 / all ticks.

choice.rule: lowest camera objective; within 0.5 deg of it, the widest deadband, then the shortest filter

power.note: criterion (a)'s camera - truth_lag CI half-width on val, scaled by sqrt(clusters): why test draws 12 starts per clip and distance, not the design's 6
